extracted.intended_audience: junior researchers asked to review machine-learning conference papers (e.g., NeurIPS / ICML / ICLR)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical walkthrough for junior ML researchers on how to read, evaluate, and write constructive reviews for top ML conferences (NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR). Covers section-by-section reading, required review components, evaluation criteria, tone, and time management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract claims verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract: note every author claim so you can verify it later in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim stated in the abstract so you can check for matching evidence later in Methods/Results. Flag any abstract claims that are unsupported or vague when writing your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: related work & positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction: identify the related works cited and the positioning relative to state-of-the-art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the authors accurately and fairly cite relevant prior work and clearly state how their contribution differs from or advances the state-of-the-art. Note missing comparisons or overstated novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods/Results: evidence for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods / Results: check that each abstract claim is supported by a corresponding piece of evidence in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each claim from the abstract/introduction, find the experimental or theoretical result that supports it. If a claim lacks direct evidence, ask for experiments, ablations, or clearer explanation. Flag unsupported claims and missing ablation studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive intent and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: View yourself as a peer advancing the field, not a superior judge. Provide positive feedback alongside criticism. Help authors improve their work rather than merely criticize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write reviews with the goal of improving the paper: acknowledge strengths, give actionable suggestions for weaknesses, avoid dismissive language. Balance negative points with explicit recognition of contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about expertise & confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Be Transparent About Expertise: Set the confidence score honestly when outside your specialization. "An unknowledgeable reviewer with high confidence is a nightmare."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your domain expertise and set any requested confidence scores honestly. When unsure about technical aspects, mark lower confidence and avoid overreaching judgments; recommend seeking additional reviewers if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: paper summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper summary (demonstrates that you understood the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the review with a concise summary in your own words to show comprehension. A good summary helps area chairs and authors see what you understood and frames the rest of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: strengths section
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the paper's positive aspects explicitly (novelty, solid experiments, clarity, strong theoretical result, etc.). Be specific rather than generic praise to make the strengths useful to authors and chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: weaknesses section
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly enumerate the paper's shortcomings (missing baselines, unclear motivation, unsupported claims, flawed evaluation). For each weakness, explain why it matters and, where possible, suggest concrete fixes or experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: detailed comments tied to concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed comments tying back to specific concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide line/section-specific or figure-specific comments that connect to the high-level strengths/weaknesses. Point to exact locations in the paper when asking for clarification or additional experiments to make revision actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required component: multiple revision passes (author recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple revision passes (the author recommends 3+ before submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although addressed to authors, reviewers should be aware that papers may improve after multiple revisions; when suggesting fixes, indicate whether they are minor (quick) or major (require several iterations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: novelty and clarity of contribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the work advances the field meaningfully and whether the contribution is clearly described. Distinguish between genuinely new ideas and incremental engineering/parameter tuning; require authors to clearly state what is new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: experimental support for every claim
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require experiments, ablations, or theoretical proofs that directly support the paper's claims. Flag claims that lack empirical verification and request appropriate additional analyses or baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: justification of design choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification of design choices ("magic numbers" should be questioned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask authors to justify hyperparameter choices, architectures, and other design decisions. Request ablation studies or sensitivity analyses when results depend on specific settings or 'magic numbers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: comparison to related work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the paper includes fair baselines and thorough comparisons to prior methods. If relevant baselines are missing, request their inclusion or reasoning for omission; check for appropriate citations and contextualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: clarity and completeness of explanations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether methods, algorithms, and proofs are explained sufficiently for reproduction/understanding. Ask for expanded derivations, pseudocode, or clarifications where exposition is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical tip: time allocation for reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan ~3 hours for an initial draft plus revision passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget time to read strategically, draft a clear summary and structured strengths/weaknesses, and perform at least one revision of your review. Use extra time to verify critical experiments or claims if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical tip: flag unsupported claims and missing ablations
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag every unsupported claim and missing ablation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically note unsupported statements and missing experimental controls/ablations in your review. Prioritize these items in your weaknesses and request specific additional experiments or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical tip: balance criticism with acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance criticism with explicit acknowledgment of contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When delivering negative feedback, also highlight what the paper does well. This helps maintain constructive tone and makes the review more helpful to authors and area chairs.
